Eighard (Eighard, H14)

Region (English scoring-table region): North Aelantir.

In one sentence: Use Autumn magic to withstand the endless winter, then decide whether to continue the Autumn Court's mission or make the whole country bow to rot.

Story: Very high ｜ Mission-tree length: Long (60 directly defined missions, including mutually exclusive routes) ｜ Mission-tree update: The current local files include the rework ｜ Uniqueness: Very high ｜ Prison-like opening: High ｜ Early pressure: Medium-high ｜ Expansion capacity: Strong. The checked version is EU4 v1.37.5.0 as supported by the base and translation Mods; file dates are not release dates.

Identity and History

Eighard is a Tuathak-elven Autumn Court theocracy in northern Eordand, with Darblath as its capital. In 1444 it is ruled by Danaran Autumnswrath, while Gemradcurt is its historical enemy; “Autumn” here is not an ordinary agricultural symbol, but a religious and survival order shaped by the long struggle against the Winter Court. [Local history script] [Local translation Mod]

Its national ideas look back on a rise and fall: for centuries Eighard held the cold northern coast with fortresses and warming magic, then gained Dorcurt's support and launched a crusade intended to end winter. The army occupied eastern lands, but when its leader, Eighard's Esbarg Andral of the Crown, demanded that his allies swear fealty, he was ambushed and killed at Minaurak. The crusading alliance broke apart; the conquered area became Jhorgashirr and Slegcal. Eighard maintained outwardly friendly relations while still seeking to recover its former leadership. The text gives no reliable year for the ambush, so no date is added. [Local flavour text]

The opening is therefore not a powerful country that already rules the Autumn Court, but a religious state restarting with lost prestige, former allies, and a Winter Court enemy. The retrospective account of the Cult of Rot taking power in the ideas cannot override the current mission choice to accept or refuse it; it cannot be used to claim that the cult has already seized power in 1444.

National Story and Campaign Arc

The early game revolves around restoring northern influence, overcoming the cold, finding iron, and establishing outposts. Ships from Cannor make the country confront the world beyond the sea more directly for the first time: there are opportunities for contact, but also colonists competing for its homeland and coasts. Cold-weather technology gradually changes from a tool for protecting cities into the foundation for pushing into winter lands. [Local flavour text]

The real turning point is the Cult of Rot. It treats the natural decomposition of autumn leaves as a justification for rule and punishment, and demands control of the country; accepting sets the cult-route flag, restricts government changes, and brings revolts by opponents. Refusing removes the infiltrated church's privileges and continues another route at the cost of the ruler's death. This is not a simple bonus button, but a political choice that determines later missions and formation eligibility. [Local script]

Those who accept continue Eighard's own long route, later changing its name under the same Tag to Liughagcal and eventually to Banoghard. Those who refuse may still meet the general conditions to form Eordand; the two endings cannot be combined without conditions in one campaign. Sixty is the total number of directly defined missions, not a claim that both mutually exclusive routes are visible at once. [Local script]

Core Mechanics

The first is cold resistance and the Warming Ritual. The story explains that the early ritual required twelve Druids to cast continuously; later attempts use the energy of decomposed matter to sustain the spell and build cold-weather outposts. Current missions also organize progress around ice protection, warming hubs, and northern administration. These systems support actual occupation and colonization, rather than serving as decoration for an “Autumn” theme. [Local flavour text] [Local script]

The second is the support/refusal count for the Cult of Rot and the route switch. Political choices steer the cult's direction; the acceptance flag changes the mission group and closes the general Eordand formation entrance. The third is a set of special magical projects whose stages connect to war, mage towers, development in specified provinces, and northern control. A powerful mage does not complete the projects automatically; the unverified total cost, timers, and penalties of the third-stage work are not given numeric values here. [Local script]

The fourth is the infrastructure chain for cold-weather expansion. Iron, outposts, navy, and colonization share the cost of advancing north. The player must check spell-research and facility prerequisites in advance rather than preparing only after the territory is occupied.

Phased Play and End States

At the start, stabilize the Autumn Court's position, develop the cold-weather foundations, and prepare for war with the Winter Court; former allies are not permanently reliable. In the middle game, advance northern expansion, iron, mage research, and colonial outposts together. Before accepting the cult, confirm which end state you want to preserve.

If the Rot route continues, expand its order under the name Banoghard; if the Eordand route is chosen, the country must not have accepted Rot and must then meet general culture, territory, and technology conditions, changing to H21 and replacing the mission tree. The former is a same-country renaming; the latter is a true formable country. [Local decision] [Local event]

The offline Wiki timeline also records Autumn Court conquests in 1589 and 1628 and the end of the crusades in 1713. These are later events in the Wiki setting, not a player mission timetable and not an inevitable future for every route. [Wiki source]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 91/100 ｜ Authoritarianism 94/100 ｜ Magic ↔ Artifice 98/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 96/100) ｜ Pluralism 12/100. The phase change is: Autumn Court defence and reconstruction (Expansion 75, Authoritarianism 65, Magic ↔ Artifice 82, magic/artifice intensity 78, Pluralism 35) → refusing the Rot route (Expansion 80, Authoritarianism 65, Magic ↔ Artifice 88, magic/artifice intensity 85, Pluralism 35).

The v2.1 value assessment is Evil (22/100), with branch alternatives rather than a sequential trajectory: the early Autumn Court defence and reconstruction calibration is Neutral 55/100; accepting the Cult of Rot is Evil 22/100; refusing the cult is provisionally Neutral 60/100. Acceptance and refusal are mutually alternative routes, not successive stages of one campaign path.

The primary coordinates, Expansion 91 / Authoritarianism 94 / magic direction 98 (intensity 96) / Pluralism 12, describe the Rot-extension route; the earlier Autumn Court defence phase remains separately recorded. The country tightly binds magic, cult politics, and northern expansion, ultimately producing a highly centralized and exclusionary order.

The value score is Evil 22: dignity 16, public benefit 40, recognition of personhood 16, restraint 16. The low score is based on the ideas explicitly placing heretics and prisoners in pits until they die and rot, displaying bones as intimidation, and the cult's seizure of power through death threats. It is not deducted merely for theocracy, the Autumn Court, war, or decomposition magic. Cold-weather protection has a limited public benefit, but does not cancel concrete violations of personhood. The early score of 55, Rot score of 22, and provisional refusal-route score of 60 express a divergence, not script-internal values; refusal does not prove that every persecution has disappeared.

This suits players who enjoy religious divergence, dark magic, northern expansion, and long character/state transformations. It is a poor fit for players who dislike colonial waiting, spell-research prerequisites, or playing a terrifying cult.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundary

Official Dev Diary 110 introduces the Eighard rework and its two directions. A report dated 18 August 2026 praises the corruption narrative but points to mid-game colonization and conversion waits; a discussion dated 15 May 2026 uses Eighard as an example of mage-research choices that can stall later mission progress. Neither post supplies an exact version, and fixes described by developers belong to development builds and cannot automatically be treated as present in the local files. [Official developer diary] [Community view]

No dedicated Eighard, Banoghard, or independent Eordand-country Wiki page was obtained. The adopted timeline range, formation conditions, and unverified project details are recorded in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Eighard (H14) — Eighard Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = H14
    }

Traditions: Eighard Traditions

Effects: Army morale: +10%; Fort defense: +10%.

Idea 1: Vanguard of the Hibernal Crusade

The cold shores of the northern Fogharabh have long been a battleground between the Autumn and Winter Courts, but until the Hibernal Crusade only the city of Darblath and a few other possessions could remain under the hands of the Tuathak. Eighard stood as the bulwark of the Autumn Court against the unrelenting wintry winds for centuries, until matters of fate thrust them into greatness. Their hated enemies, the Snecboth, were lulled into a feeling of false safety, believing that they had nothing to fear from the Tuathak who cowered in their fortresses until the end of winter. Eighard developed a plan, gathering support from the old Autumn Court of Dorcurt and gathering a vast army of the faithful. A holy war to end the Winter once and for all was declared: once the Snecboth and their lands were conquered by Eighard and their allies, they could end their idolatry and cease the hated season forever!

The Hibernal Crusade won victory after victory, crushing the Winter Court and seizing the lands eastward towards what would become Jhorgashirr and Slegcal. All that remained was Gemradcurt, but the Esbagg of Eighard, Andrall Harvestcrown, knew that their allies would seize their conquered lands and sought to force their loyalty at Minnorac, the Field of Oaths. This proved to be a cataclysmic mistake, for they were ambushed there by the Strutmar Peitar and the unity of the Hibernal Crusade was shattered with the death of Esbagg Andrall Harvestcrown.

Following the ambush at Minnorac, the remaining leadership of the Hibernal Crusade rushed to consolidate power and seized control of the conquered lands, forming the traitorous states of Jhorgashirr and Slegcal. While Eigharders view them as deserters, they do not show this openly, and their government has maintained friendly relations with them in a vain attempt to regain the influence they once held.

Effects: Diplomatic relations: +1.

Idea 2: Warmth Rites

Battered by the incessant frigid winds and waves, Darblath is a cold and mirthless place. Yet, it could be worse, for the hardships the Eigharders face have bestowed unto them unique spells and incantations. The traditional magical arts of the Autumn Court have been mastered and redefined: although all things must change like how the leaves change in the end of Autumn, perhaps it could be put off until later. The Warmth Rites were some of the first Eigharder spells, requiring intense and uninterrupted concentration by a team of no less than twelve druids. Over many years the Warmth Rites have acted as a ward against the cold, but have never been enough to keep old Winter at bay.

Effects: Missionaries: +1.

Idea 3: Icewardery of Darblath

The second magical innovation of Eighard has permitted their Tuathak Legions to persist in the desolate northern wilderness. Only at the Icewardery of Darblath, a secluded building guarded far behind the Esbagg's fortress, are these enchantments prepared to ensure the exclusivity of their technique continues. Icewarded equipment often appear plain at first sight, no different from common armor, but beneath its surface are revealed a gleaming sheen on scratches or splinters. Donning icewarded equipment produces a warming effect on the wearer: while not enough to allow unlimited action in freezing temperatures, it is enough to permit Eighard's legions full ability to complete their complex and successful maneuvers.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 4: Hibernal Requisitions

The eternal struggle against the hated Winter has required an iron grip on all available resources, spurring the creation of the Hibernal Requisitions doctrine. During wartime, the Esbagg of Eighard may seize anything that is required for the war effort on the condition that the land or resource is returned or repaid, but any suspected cases of heresy will be dealt with harshly. When in Eighard it is wise to willingly surrender anything required for the Hibernal Requisition, as throughout its many years of usage almost all who refuse have been found and executed as Wintry informants.

Effects: global_autonomy：-0.05%.

Idea 5: Dour Dyes

The bleak weather of Darblath harbor is reflected in its chief export: muted gray, blue, and brown dyes. The boreal hinterlands provide a bountiful source of these dyes, crushed from bark and squeezed from soil in stinking vats. These muted colors have become a proud heritage of Eigharders, claiming that it shows their humility and practicality. However, they are quick to boast that their dyes are far superior, and more plentiful, than Sglard's foppish bright dyes, not to even mention the garish pink of Dearktir!

Effects: Trade efficiency: +10%.

Idea 6: The Boreal Vigilance Corps

The backcountry roads, practically anywhere outside of Darblath and its immediate environs, are haunted by raiding Snecboth who threaten our very existence. Mobilizing the army against such threats is impractical, for they melt away into the frozen woods at the blink of an eye, and return just as quickly. To face such a threat the Boreal Vigilance Corps was established, composed of junior regiments that receive their training by patrolling the roadways.

Effects: Manpower recovery speed: +15%.

Idea 7: The Cult of Rot

Unending strife and hatred over many generations is not conducive to creating a welcoming and friendly society. Unable to back down from war with the Wintry heretics, many in Eighard have taken to extreme measures to ensure victory. The Cult of Rot upholds the nature of decay of fallen Autumn leaves, viewing that as the ultimate and just punishment for those sentenced to execution. At first viewed as a troublesome but unimportant heretical cult by the mainstream Autumn Court who favor the aspect of Autumn as the season of harvest and preparation, the Cult of Rot seized control of Eighard overtime, slowly replacing the governorship until even their Esbagg adhered to their practices.

Their most infamous practice was the construction of a new prison in Darblath, a squat but deep building extending far into the earth, where heretics and prisoners were locked in pit-like cells and left until their body decayed into soil. The many bones left behind were showcased as a warning to would-be troublemakers, with some thrown into a massive pile outside the prison as example, and others left in a long corridor all over the floor and walls where domestic and foreign dignitaries were reminded of their fate should they fail.

Effects: Maximum Absolutism: +10; Yearly absolutism: +0.5.

Ambition: Eighard Ambition

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Eordand (H21) — Eordan Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = H21
    }

Traditions: Eordan Traditions

Effects: True faith tolerance: +2; Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 1: Unification of Eordand

Eordand united, the four seasons for the first time stride in unison. However, not all submit to our rule. In the hinterlands and even amongst our cities there are those who would dare question our authority, and wish for a return to the supremacy of one season. We must do all we can to stop these dissidents and preserve our union.

Effects: Stability cost modifier: -15%; Autonomy change cooldown: raw value -0.1 (unit unverified).

Idea 2: Eordan Expeditions

In the past the expeditions of the Eordan faith only retrieved Precursor artifacts from dangerous locations. In the present, further steps must be taken to secure our access to artifacts. All locations with possible Precursor artifacts must be fortified with the Eordan faith!

Effects: Colonists: +1; Settler chance: +10%.

Idea 3: Domandrod Lightbringers

Zealots of the Eordellon faith, the Domandrod Lightbringers are those who spent years stalking the Domandrod with the Fey Lords themselves. These Lightbringers, thankfully, see us as the chosen heirs of Eordand, and will unfalteringly serve us. They will bring to the enemy death in sword, magic and shot.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 4: Rekindled Precursor Ruins

Eordand is replete with Precursor ruins, many of them still somewhat intact. For centuries our people dwelt within these ruins, mere squatters compared to our majesty today. The Ruins are ruined no longer, restored to at least some semblance of their lost glory.

Effects: Technology cost: -10%.

Idea 5: Heirs to the Precursor Empire

As one of the sole survivors of the Day of Ashen Skies, Eordand has returned from the grave. All around us the Ruinborn and Cannorians squabble over the land and the few ruins, but it is Eordand that are the true heirs to these lands. None shall hold us back from what is our destiny!

Effects: Prestige: +0.5; Legitimacy: +0.5; Republican tradition: +0.3; Devotion: +0.5; Horde unity: +0.5.

Idea 6: A Light in the West

Despite the faltering of our neighbours, they are still our cousins. Be they the Ynnic, Alecandi or even the Cursed Ones, our brethren all need our protection from the Outsiders. The Eordan faith will protect them, and they will see the wisdom that comes from the seasons and the Fey.

Effects: Missionary strength: +2%.

Idea 7: Eordan Artificery

Independent or parallel to the Cannorian artificery, Eordand channeled magic into items at power no less. With these inventions, our industries are far more efficient in all fields. Eordan products, even magirifles, should be shipped across the world, for it is best for others to be dependent on us.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Ambition: Eordan Ambition

Effects: Army tradition from battles: +1.
